levels.name: A1 — Absolute Beginner
levels.description: Alphabet, pronunciation, gender, basic sentences, the present tense.

levels.name: A2 — Elementary
levels.description: All six cases at an introductory level, past and future tense, aspect basics, full adjective agreement.

levels.name: B1 — Intermediate
levels.description: Motion verbs, complex sentences, reflexives, imperatives, reported speech, conditionals.

levels.name: B2 — Upper Intermediate
levels.description: Numeral grammar in depth, participles, gerunds, more aspect nuance.

levels.name: C1 — Advanced
levels.description: Discourse particles, registers, derivational prefixes, impersonal constructions, advanced aspect.

levels.name: C2 — Mastery
levels.description: Archaic and literary grammar, Church Slavonic influence, poetic inversion, regionalisms, idiom.

topics.title: Cyrillic Alphabet
topics.subtitle: The first wall every learner climbs.

sections.heading: What to learn
items: Printed letters
Handwritten letters (critical — Russian cursive looks very different from print)
Upper and lowercase forms

sections.heading: Letters that trip up English speakers
items: Д д — looks unfamiliar in cursive
Т т — cursive т looks like English m
Г г — cursive г looks like English z
Л л — easy to confuse with П in cursive

sections.heading: False-friend letters
items: Р reads as R (not P)
С reads as S (not C)
Н reads as N (not H)
В reads as V (not B)
У reads as U (not Y)

topics.title: Pronunciation Fundamentals
topics.subtitle: The sounds that don't exist in English.

sections.heading: Core topics
items: Hard vs soft consonants
Stress (unmarked in writing; you have to learn each word's stress)
Vowel reduction (unstressed о → a-sound)
Consonant devoicing (final voiced consonants devoice: хлеб → хлеп)
Pronunciation of ы (no English equivalent)
Soft sign ь (palatalizes the consonant before it)
Hard sign ъ (separates prefix from soft vowel)

sections.heading: How to practice
items: Minimal pairs (брат vs брать)
Shadowing native audio
Reading aloud daily

topics.title: Basic Sentence Structure
topics.subtitle: Russian skips 'to be' in the present tense.

sections.heading: Core rule
items: Subject + verb is the default word order, but Russian is flexible
In present tense, the verb 'to be' (быть) is omitted
Я студент = 'I am a student' — literally just 'I student'

topics.title: Personal Pronouns
topics.subtitle: The seven words that start every Russian conversation.

sections.heading: The pronouns
items: я — I
ты — you (singular, informal)
он — he / it (masculine)
она — she / it (feminine)
оно — it (neuter)
мы — we
вы — you (plural OR formal singular)
они — they

sections.heading: Note
items: ты vs вы matters socially — вы to strangers, elders, in formal situations
Russian pronouns decline through all six cases (you'll meet meня, мне, мной soon enough)

topics.title: Present Tense Verbs
topics.subtitle: Two conjugation patterns and a handful of stubborn irregulars.

sections.heading: Core topics
items: Infinitives end in -ть (мостly), -ти, or -чь
First conjugation (-е- type): читать → читаю, читаешь, читает...
Second conjugation (-и- type): говорить → говорю, говоришь, говорит...
Common irregular verbs you must memorize

sections.heading: Core verbs to learn first
items: быть — to be (used only outside present)
жить — to live
работать — to work
знать — to know
понимать — to understand
говорить — to speak / say
хотеть — to want (irregular!)
мочь — can / be able to (irregular!)

topics.title: Gender
topics.subtitle: Every noun is one of three. Endings give it away.

sections.heading: The three genders (+ plural)
items: Masculine — usually ends in a consonant or -й
Feminine — usually ends in -а or -я
Neuter — usually ends in -о or -е
Plural is a separate agreement category, not a fourth gender

sections.heading: Trap
items: Nouns ending in -ь can be EITHER masculine or feminine — you have to memorize each one (день m., ночь f.)

topics.title: Numbers (basics)
topics.subtitle: Counting, time, age, dates. The hard part comes later (B2).

sections.heading: Topics
items: Cardinal numbers 0–100
Time expressions (сейчас час, два часа, три часа, пять часов...)
Age expressions (мне 30 лет)
Dates (Сегодня третье октября.)

sections.heading: Warning
items: Numbers force surrounding nouns into specific cases — but you don't need to master that until B2. For now just learn the words.

topics.title: Question Formation
topics.subtitle: Yes/no via intonation; wh-questions via question words.

sections.heading: Question words
items: Кто? — who?
Что? — what?
Где? — where?
Когда? — when?
Почему? — why?
Как? — how?
Сколько? — how much / many?
Какой? — what kind / which? (agrees in gender)

sections.heading: Yes/no questions
items: No word order change needed — just rising intonation on the questioned word
Ты студент? = 'Are you a student?' (compare Ты студент. = 'You are a student.')

topics.title: Negation
topics.subtitle: не before the word being negated; нет for 'there isn't'.

sections.heading: Two key words
items: не — 'not' (placed directly before whatever you're negating)
нет — 'no' (one-word answer) AND 'there is not' (followed by genitive)

sections.heading: Negative pronouns
items: никто — nobody
ничего — nothing
никогда — never
нигде — nowhere
никуда — to nowhere

items.en: Nobody knows anything (lit. nobody nothing not knows).

sections.heading: Watch out
items: Russian uses DOUBLE NEGATIVES — both the negative pronoun AND не are required (Никто не знает, never just Никто знает).

topics.title: Nominative Case
topics.subtitle: The default. Subject of the sentence; dictionary form.

sections.heading: Functions
items: Subject of the sentence
Predicate nouns after 'to be' in present (Это книга.)
The form you'll find in any dictionary

sections.heading: Related topics to study together
items: Noun gender
Plural formation
Adjective agreement (gender, number, case all match the noun)

items.en: A beautiful house stands on the hill.

topics.title: Accusative Case
topics.subtitle: Direct object of a transitive verb.

sections.heading: Functions
items: Direct object: Я вижу брата.
Motion 'into' or 'onto' with в/на: Я иду в школу.

sections.heading: Big rule: animacy matters
items: Masculine ANIMATE nouns take genitive-shaped endings in accusative (брат → брата)
Masculine INANIMATE nouns look identical to nominative (стол → стол)
Feminine -а/-я → -у/-ю regardless of animacy (книга → книгу)
Neuter looks identical to nominative

items.en: I see the table. (inanimate, no change)

topics.title: Prepositional Case
topics.subtitle: Location, and what you're talking about.

sections.heading: Functions
items: Location with в (in) and на (on/at): в Москве, на работе
'About' with о/об/обо: о книге

sections.heading: Endings (singular)
items: Masc / Neut → -е (most nouns)
Fem -а/-я → -е (книга → о книге)
Fem -ь → -и (ночь → о ночи)
Words in -ия, -ие, -ий → -ии

topics.title: Genitive Case
topics.subtitle: The most-used case in Russian — and its plural is a famous nightmare.

sections.heading: Functions
items: Possession: книга брата ('brother's book')
Absence: нет времени ('no time')
Quantity: много людей ('many people')
Negation of an object: Я не знаю ответа.
After numbers 2–4 (singular genitive) and 5+ (plural genitive)
After most prepositions of place/source: из, от, у, без

sections.heading: Endings (singular)
items: Masc / Neut → -а / -я
Fem -а/-я → -ы / -и

sections.heading: Genitive plural — the famous trap
items: Masc nouns → -ов / -ев / -ей
Fem nouns ending in -а → drop the ending (книга → книг)
Neuter nouns → drop the ending (окно → окон)
Many words insert a 'fleeting vowel': окно → окон, девушка → девушек

topics.title: Dative Case
topics.subtitle: Indirect object — the recipient. Also age and feelings.

sections.heading: Functions
items: Indirect object: Я дал другу книгу.
Age: Мне двадцать лет.
Physical/emotional states: Мне холодно. Мне скучно.
Recipient of giving/showing/telling verbs

sections.heading: Constructions to memorize
items: Мне нравится X — 'I like X' (literally: X is pleasing to me)
Мне нужно — 'I need to'
Мне можно? — 'May I?'
Мне кажется — 'It seems to me'

items.en: I'm cold (lit. it is cold to me).
I gave my friend a book.

topics.title: Instrumental Case
topics.subtitle: 'With' / 'by means of' / what someone IS (profession).

sections.heading: Functions
items: With (accompaniment), using с: с другом
By means of (no preposition): писать ручкой ('writing with a pen')
Profession: работать врачом ('working as a doctor')
After certain verbs (заниматься, интересоваться, гордиться)

topics.title: Past Tense
topics.subtitle: Easier than the present tense — it agrees with gender, not person.

sections.heading: How it works
items: Drop the -ть from the infinitive and add: -л (masc), -ла (fem), -ло (neuter), -ли (plural)
The past tense agrees with the SUBJECT'S gender, not the speaker's
Some verbs have irregular stems (мочь → мог, идти → шёл)

items.en: I didn't know (said by a male).
I didn't know (said by a female).

topics.title: Future Tense
topics.subtitle: Two flavors — imperfective and perfective.

sections.heading: Imperfective future (process / ongoing future action)
items: Conjugate быть (буду, будешь, будет, будем, будете, будут) + imperfective infinitive
Я буду читать. = 'I will read / I will be reading.'

sections.heading: Perfective future (single completed future action)
items: Take the perfective verb and conjugate it in 'present' form — the meaning is automatically future
Я прочитаю. = 'I will read (and finish).'

items.ru: Завтра я буду работать весь день.
items.en: Tomorrow I'll be working all day.
I'll read the book (cover to cover) in a week.

topics.title: Verb Aspect — Introduction
topics.subtitle: Probably the most important grammatical concept in Russian.

sections.heading: The core distinction
items: IMPERFECTIVE: process, repetition, or ongoing action. Answers 'what was happening?'
PERFECTIVE: completed action, single event, with a result. Answers 'what happened (and got done)?'

sections.heading: Aspect pairs
items: Most verbs come in pairs — same meaning, different aspect
делать / сделать — to do / to complete doing
писать / написать — to write / to finish writing
читать / прочитать — to read / to read through

sections.heading: Practice
items: Time expressions: 'I read for an hour' (imperf) vs 'I read a book in an hour' (perf)
Sequencing: 'When I had finished (perf), I left (perf)'
Intentions: 'I'm going to write' (imperf — general intention) vs 'I will write and send it' (perf)

items.en: I was writing the letter for an hour. (imperf — process)
I wrote (completed) the letter in an hour. (perf — result)

topics.title: Full Adjective Declension
topics.subtitle: Adjectives match the noun in gender, number, AND case.

sections.heading: Triple agreement
items: Gender — masc / fem / neut
Number — singular / plural
Case — all six

sections.heading: Nominative endings
items: Masc: -ый / -ий / -ой (новый, синий, большой)
Fem: -ая / -яя (новая, синяя)
Neut: -ое / -ее (новое, синее)
Plural: -ые / -ие (новые, синие)

items.en: new house → in the new house
beautiful book → (I see) the beautiful book

topics.title: Possessive Pronouns
topics.subtitle: мой / твой / наш / ваш — agree with the noun like adjectives. Он/она/они are invariable.

sections.heading: The forms (nominative)
items: мой / моя / моё / мои — my
твой / твоя / твоё / твои — your (sg.)
наш / наша / наше / наши — our
ваш / ваша / ваше / ваши — your (pl./formal)
его / её / их — his / her / their (NEVER change form)

topics.title: Demonstratives — этот / тот
topics.subtitle: 'This' vs 'that'. Both decline like adjectives.

sections.heading: The forms (nominative)
items: этот / эта / это / эти — this / these
тот / та / то / те — that / those

topics.title: Comparatives & Superlatives
topics.subtitle: 'Better', 'more interesting', 'the most beautiful'.

sections.heading: Simple comparatives (invariable)
items: лучше — better
хуже — worse
больше — more / bigger
меньше — less / smaller
Used predicatively: Эта книга интереснее.

sections.heading: Compound comparatives
items: более + adjective — more X
менее + adjective — less X
Used attributively: более интересный фильм

sections.heading: Superlatives
items: самый + adjective — the most X (most common, declines normally)
самый красивый — the most beautiful
Some have synthetic forms: лучший (best), худший (worst)

items.en: This is the most beautiful city.

topics.title: Motion Verbs — Basic Pairs
topics.subtitle: Russian distinguishes HOW you go before WHERE you go.

sections.heading: The three core pairs
items: On foot: идти / ходить
By transport: ехать / ездить
Carrying: нести / носить

sections.heading: Other useful pairs
items: лететь / летать — to fly
плыть / плавать — to swim / sail
бежать / бегать — to run
вести / водить — to lead / drive (someone)
везти / возить — to transport

items.en: I'm going (right now, on foot) to school.

items.ru: Я хожу в школу каждый день.
items.en: I go to school every day.

topics.title: Motion — Unidirectional vs Multidirectional
topics.subtitle: Two imperfectives for the same verb. The brain rebels.

sections.heading: The distinction
items: UNIDIRECTIONAL (идти, ехать, лететь) — going in one direction, right now, or a planned single trip
MULTIDIRECTIONAL (ходить, ездить, летать) — habitual, repeated, round-trip, random wandering, OR ability

items.ru: Я хожу в спортзал три раза в неделю. (repeated)
items.en: I go to the gym 3 times a week.

items.ru: Вчера я ходил в кино. (round trip — went and came back)
items.en: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

topics.title: Motion Prefixes
topics.subtitle: Stick a prefix on a motion verb and you get a perfective with a specific direction.

sections.heading: Common prefixes
items: при- (arrival): прийти — to arrive
у- (departure): уйти — to leave
в- (entry): войти — to enter
вы- (exit): выйти — to exit
пере- (crossing / across): перейти — to cross
до- (reaching a point): дойти — to reach
об- (around): обойти — to go around
под- (approaching): подойти — to approach
от- (away from): отойти — to step away

topics.title: Motion Verbs + Aspect
topics.subtitle: Adding a prefix turns idti/ekhat' into a perfective. The multidirectionals stay imperfective.

sections.heading: The pattern
items: Unidirectional + prefix = perfective (uses the unidirectional stem)
Multidirectional + prefix = imperfective partner to that perfective
Example: prefix при- + идти/ходить → прийти (pf) / приходить (impf)

topics.title: Conjunctions — Building Complex Sentences
topics.subtitle: The connectors that turn a beginner into someone who can argue.

sections.heading: Core conjunctions
items: потому что — because
так что — so / therefore
если — if
хотя — although
чтобы — in order to / so that (always followed by past or infinitive)
когда — when
пока — while / until
поэтому — therefore

items.ru: Я не пошёл, потому что было холодно.
items.en: I didn't go because it was cold.

items.ru: Я учу русский, чтобы читать Достоевского.
items.en: I'm learning Russian in order to read Dostoevsky.

items.ru: Хотя было холодно, я пошёл гулять.
items.en: Although it was cold, I went for a walk.

topics.title: Relative Clauses — который
topics.subtitle: 'который' is the workhorse 'who/which/that' — and it declines.

sections.heading: How it works
items: который agrees with its antecedent in GENDER and NUMBER
Its CASE is determined by its role in the relative clause, NOT by the antecedent
Always preceded by a comma

items.en: The person who lives here is a doctor.

items.ru: Книга, которую я читаю, очень интересная.
items.en: The book (which) I'm reading is very interesting.

items.ru: Друг, с которым я говорил, уехал.
items.en: The friend (with whom) I was speaking has left.

topics.title: Reported Speech
topics.subtitle: Russian keeps the original tense. No backshift like in English.

sections.heading: The key difference from English
items: English: He said he WAS tired. (past → past-shifted)
Russian: Он сказал, что он устал. (literally 'he said that he is tired')
Russian tenses don't shift in indirect speech — the verb stays in the tense it was originally in

items.en: He said that he is working / was working.
She said she would come tomorrow. (literally 'will come')

topics.title: Conditional Sentences — если бы
topics.subtitle: Hypotheticals always use 'бы + past tense'.

sections.heading: Real vs hypothetical
items: REAL conditional (just 'если'): Если будет дождь, я останусь дома.
HYPOTHETICAL (если бы + past): Если бы у меня было время, я бы пошёл.
Note: бы appears in BOTH halves of a hypothetical

items.ru: Если бы я знал, я бы сказал тебе.
items.en: If I had known, I would have told you.

items.ru: Если будет хорошая погода, мы поедем за город.
items.en: If the weather is good, we'll go to the countryside.

topics.title: Word Order Nuance
topics.subtitle: Russian word order is flexible, but not random. Position carries information.

sections.heading: The principle
items: New information tends to go at the END of the sentence
Topic (what's being discussed) tends to come first; focus (the new thing) comes last
Moving a word forward EMPHASIZES or contrasts it

items.en: You — I love (it's YOU I love, not someone else).

sections.heading: Note
items: Same dictionary meaning, very different emotional focus. This is what makes translating Russian poetry into English so brutal.

topics.title: Reflexive Verbs (-ся / -сь)
topics.subtitle: Reflexive in form, but only sometimes reflexive in meaning.

sections.heading: Three meanings
items: True reflexive (action on self): мыться — to wash oneself
Reciprocal (each other): встречаться — to meet each other
Passive-like (no doer): дверь открывается — the door opens
Lexicalized — the -ся version has its own meaning: учить (to teach) vs учиться (to study)

sections.heading: Common reflexive verbs
items: учиться — to study
заниматься — to be busy with / to study (a subject)
бояться — to be afraid (takes genitive)
находиться — to be located
родиться — to be born
смеяться — to laugh
нравиться — to be pleasing (used in мне нравится)

items.en: I'm afraid of the dark. (genitive after бояться)

topics.title: Imperatives
topics.subtitle: Commands — informal (ты) and formal/plural (вы).

sections.heading: Formation
items: Take the present-tense они form, drop the ending, add -й/-и/-ь
читают → читай (informal) / читайте (formal)
говорят → говори / говорите
Aspect matters: imperfective for invitations and ongoing, perfective for single completed asks

items.en: Read this book. (imperf — read it / be reading it)

topics.title: Cardinal Numerals — Deep Dive
topics.subtitle: Russian numerals decline AND they control the case of the noun they count. Famous misery.

sections.heading: The rules for what follows a number
items: 1 (один) + nominative singular: один стол
2, 3, 4 + genitive singular: два стола, три стола
5–20 + genitive plural: пять столов
Compound numbers go by the LAST digit: 22 = 'двадцать два стола' (last digit 2 → gen sg)
11–14 are exceptions — always gen plural (одиннадцать столов)

topics.title: Ordinal Numerals
topics.subtitle: 'First', 'second', 'third' — these behave like adjectives.

sections.heading: Key forms
items: первый — first
второй — second
третий — third (irregular declension!)
четвёртый — fourth
пятый — fifth
Ordinals agree with their noun in gender, number, case — just like adjectives

items.en: Today is the third of October. (neuter, agreeing with implicit число)

topics.title: Collective Numerals
topics.subtitle: двое, трое, четверо — used with groups of (usually male) people.

sections.heading: The forms
items: двое — two (as a group)
трое — three
четверо — four
пятеро — five
Used with mixed-gender groups, groups of children, and certain plural-only nouns

items.en: Two men stood by the door.
A day went by. Two days went by. (сутки is plural-only — needs a collective)

topics.title: Numerals + Case Interaction
topics.subtitle: Numbers themselves decline. Throw them into the dative and feel the pain.

sections.heading: Key fact
items: In oblique cases (anything except nom/acc), the NUMBER takes the case AND so does the noun — both in the same case, same number
пять домов (nom/acc, gen pl) → к пяти домам (dat, dat pl) → с пятью домами (instr, instr pl)

items.en: I was with three friends. (instr — both number and noun in instr)

items.ru: Полтора часа = an hour and a half (полтора itself is irregular)

topics.title: Present Active Participles
topics.subtitle: 'The person doing X' — formed from imperfective verbs.

sections.heading: Formation
items: Take они form, drop the -т, add -щий (declines like adjective)
читают → читающий — 'reading' / 'one who is reading'
Largely literary / journalistic. Spoken Russian prefers 'который' clauses.

items.en: The man reading the newspaper is my uncle.

items.ru: = Человек, который читает газету, — мой дядя.

topics.title: Past Active Participles
topics.subtitle: 'The person who was doing / who did X'.

sections.heading: Formation
items: From past-tense stem: читал → читавший
From perfective: прочитал → прочитавший
Highly literary. Tolstoy and bureaucrats love these.

items.ru: Человек, написавший это письмо, — мой брат.
items.en: The man who wrote this letter is my brother.

items.ru: Студент, изучавший русский, поехал в Москву.
items.en: The student who was studying Russian went to Moscow.

topics.title: Present Passive Participles
topics.subtitle: 'The thing being X-ed' — often shows up as an adjective.

sections.heading: Formation
items: Add -м- to the present stem: читаемый — '(being) read'
Rare in spoken Russian; common in technical and academic writing

topics.title: Past Passive Participles
topics.subtitle: 'The thing that has been X-ed' — extremely common.

sections.heading: Formation
items: From perfective verbs: прочитанный, написанный, открытый, закрытый
Two endings: -нный (most verbs) or -тый (some verbs)
Has a short form used predicatively: книга прочитана

items.en: a book that's been read (long form, attributive)
The book has been read. (short form, predicate)

topics.title: Imperfective Gerunds (деепричастия)
topics.subtitle: 'While X-ing' — a simultaneous action.

sections.heading: Formation
items: Drop -ют/-ут from они form, add -я (or -а after hissing consonants)
читают → читая
Express action happening AT THE SAME TIME as the main verb
Subject must be the same as the main clause

items.en: While reading the book, he fell asleep.

items.ru: Гуляя по парку, я думал о тебе.
items.en: Walking through the park, I was thinking about you.

topics.title: Perfective Gerunds
topics.subtitle: 'Having X-ed' — a completed prior action.

sections.heading: Formation
items: Take perfective past-tense stem, add -в (or -вши)
сделал → сделав
Express action that HAS BEEN COMPLETED before the main verb's action begins

items.en: Having done his homework, he went for a walk.
Having read the letter, she cried.

topics.title: Aspect — Iterative Meaning
topics.subtitle: Repeated completed actions: 'I read each one' vs 'I read for a while each time'.

sections.heading: The nuance
items: Imperfective for repeated events seen as a habit or pattern
Perfective is generally avoided for repetition — except in specific iterative constructions
Specific verbs like бывать (a 'multifrequentative' of быть) carry built-in repetition

items.en: I used to be in Moscow often. (iterative imperfective)

items.ru: Каждый раз, когда он приходил, он приносил цветы.
items.en: Every time he came, he brought flowers.

topics.title: Delimitative Verbs (по-)
topics.subtitle: 'To X for a little while' — bounded perfective with the prefix по-.

sections.heading: The pattern
items: Prefix по- on an imperfective gives a perfective meaning 'do X for a limited time'
почитать = 'to read for a bit'
поспать = 'to take a nap'
погулять = 'to take a walk'
Different from the result-focused perfective

items.en: I read for a bit and went to sleep.

topics.title: Semelfactive Verbs (-ну-)
topics.subtitle: 'To X once, briefly' — a single instantaneous occurrence.

sections.heading: The pattern
items: Suffix -ну- on certain verbs gives a one-shot, instantaneous meaning
крикнуть — to shout once (vs кричать, to be shouting)
толкнуть — to push once
вздохнуть — to give a single sigh

topics.title: Ingressive Meaning (за-)
topics.subtitle: 'To begin X-ing' — the prefix за- marks the start of an action.

sections.heading: The pattern
items: Prefix за- on certain verbs marks the BEGINNING of an action
заговорить — to start speaking
запеть — to start singing
заплакать — to start crying

topics.title: Discourse Particles
topics.subtitle: Tiny words. Enormous emotional payload. Translators despair.

sections.heading: The main offenders
items: же — emphasis / contrast / 'but really'
ведь — 'after all' / appealing to shared knowledge
бы — hypothetical / softening / wish
ли — yes/no question marker (especially in indirect questions)
мол / дескать — 'so they say' / signaling reported / often skeptical speech
то — emphatic / specifying (this, of all things)
вот — 'here' / pointing / introducing

items.en: He, supposedly, is not at fault. (мол = quoting skeptically)
I, for one, know. (то = emphatic specifying)

topics.title: Conditional Mood (бы + past)
topics.subtitle: Softening, wishing, and counterfactuals.

sections.heading: How it works
items: бы + past tense forms the conditional / subjunctive mood
Used for hypotheticals (если бы...), wishes (хотел бы...), polite requests (не могли бы вы...)
бы can move around but typically follows the first stressed word

items.en: I would go, but I'm tired.
I wish I knew (lit. 'I would want to know').

items.ru: Не могли бы вы мне помочь?
items.en: Could you (would you be able to) help me?

topics.title: Subjunctive Meanings
topics.subtitle: Wishes, desires, polite tentativeness — all driven by бы.

sections.heading: Common patterns
items: хотел бы — 'I would like'
мог бы — 'could / might'
сказал бы — 'would say'
чтобы + past — purpose / desire after verbs of wanting

items.en: I want you to come. (lit. 'I want that you would come')

topics.title: Impersonal Constructions
topics.subtitle: Sentences with no grammatical subject. Very Russian.

sections.heading: Common patterns
items: Dative + adverb: Мне холодно. (I'm cold)
Dative + verb: Мне нравится. (I like it)
Reflexive impersonals: Мне не спится. (I can't sleep)
Accusative + verb: Меня тошнит. (I feel nauseous)
Zero-subject 'natural' sentences: Светает. (It's getting light.)

topics.title: Prefixes & Verb Derivation
topics.subtitle: One base verb becomes an entire ecosystem.

sections.heading: The principle
items: Adding a prefix to a verb creates a new verb (usually perfective) with a specific shade of meaning
writing example with писать:

sections.heading: The ecosystem of писать
items: писать — to write
написать — to write (perfective; complete the writing)
подписать — to sign (under-write)
записать — to write down / record
переписать — to rewrite / copy over
выписать — to write out / extract
приписать — to attribute / write in addition
описать — to describe
расписать — to schedule / paint in detail
вписать — to write in / insert

sections.heading: Note
items: Every common Russian verb has 5–15 prefixed cousins. Once you internalize the prefix meanings, you can often GUESS what a new verb means.

topics.title: Register — Formal Russian
topics.subtitle: How educated, respectful Russian feels.

sections.heading: Markers of formal Russian
items: Use of вы (always) and full first name + patronymic
Full forms of words (нет → отсутствует in writing)
Participial and gerund constructions instead of который / когда
Loan words from Latin/Greek tend to feel more formal
Avoidance of slang, contractions, and emotional particles

items.ru: Уважаемый Иван Петрович, позвольте Вас поздравить с праздником.
items.en: Esteemed Ivan Petrovich, allow me to congratulate you on the holiday.

topics.title: Register — Conversational Russian
topics.subtitle: Real spoken Russian. Particles everywhere. Contractions of pronouns.

sections.heading: Spoken-only patterns
items: Heavy use of particles (же, вот, ну, да, ведь, типа)
Reduction of pronouns and verbs (щас for сейчас, чё for что)
Diminutives everywhere — for things AND people (Машенька, чайку)
Word order shifts to put new info at the end, regardless of 'rules'
Filler words: короче ('long story short'), кстати, кажется

topics.title: Register — Bureaucratic Russian (канцелярит)
topics.subtitle: The Soviet-flavored prose of forms, decrees, and contracts. A category of its own.

sections.heading: Hallmarks
items: Heavy use of verbal nouns ending in -ние (рассмотрение, утверждение)
Constructions like 'являться + instrumental' instead of plain 'быть'
Long chains of genitive: рассмотрение вопроса утверждения списка предприятий...
Avoidance of personal verbs; preference for passive and impersonal
Words like в соответствии с, согласно, при условии

items.ru: В соответствии с приказом № 47 от 12 марта 2024 года...
items.en: In accordance with order No. 47 dated March 12, 2024...

topics.title: Archaic Grammar
topics.subtitle: Forms you'll meet in 19th-century literature and modern poetry.

sections.heading: What to recognize
items: Vocative case fossilized in fixed phrases (Боже мой, отче)
The old aorist and imperfect tenses (no longer used, but appear in Bible / chronicles)
Short-form adjectives used attributively, not just predicatively
Older negative-with-Genitive constructions where modern Russian uses Accusative

items.ru: Отче наш, иже еси на небесех... (Lord's Prayer, Church Slavonic)
Боже мой! (vocative remnant in everyday exclamation)

topics.title: Poetic Word Order
topics.subtitle: Word order Russian poets use that prose never would.

sections.heading: Features
items: Splitting of noun phrases across verses (adjective in one line, noun in the next)
Verb-final clauses for emphasis or rhythm
Heavy use of inversion to land a key word at the line break
Archaic syntax to evoke epic or sacred registers

items.ru: Я помню чудное мгновенье... (Pushkin: 'I remember a wondrous moment')

topics.title: Church Slavonic Influence
topics.subtitle: The liturgical layer of vocabulary and morphology that elevates 'high' Russian.

sections.heading: What to look for
items: Words with -ра-/-ла- where modern Russian uses -оро-/-оло-: глава (head, elevated) vs голова (head, neutral)
Vocabulary doublets: рот (mouth, common) / уста (lips, elevated/poetic)
Old word-formation patterns: -ущий, -ющий participles trace back here

topics.title: Soviet-Era Stylistic Patterns
topics.subtitle: 20th-century registers — propaganda, samizdat, official prose.

sections.heading: Features to recognize
items: Compound abbreviations: колхоз, совхоз, ВЦСПС, КГБ — once everywhere
Heavy nominalization (verbal nouns over verbs) — already mentioned in canвцелярит
Vocabulary of struggle, building, plan, collective
Euphemism and double meaning in Soviet-era literature

items.en: comrade (Soviet honorific, now rarely used neutrally)

topics.title: Idiomatic Speech, Humor & Irony
topics.subtitle: The final frontier — implication, irony, cultural reference.

sections.heading: What you're working on at this level
items: Idioms you can't decode from the words: бить баклуши, гонять лысого, точить лясы
Cultural references — Pushkin, Soviet films, anekdoty, internet memes
Irony and sarcasm without explicit markers
Implicature — what's NOT said often carries more meaning than what is

items.en: To idle / waste time (lit. 'to hit baklushas').

topics.title: Stress Shifts
topics.subtitle: Russian stress is mobile. Same word, different case, different syllable.

sections.heading: The pain
items: Stress can move with case and number — and the pattern is not always predictable
Common pattern: stem stress in nom sg, ending stress in oblique cases
Common pattern: stem stress in singular, ending stress in plural
You ultimately have to learn the stress pattern of each word

items.ru: го́род (nom sg) → города́ (nom pl) — stress jumps
ру́ки (nom pl) → руки́ (gen sg) — stress shift between forms
items.en: hands (nom pl) / of a hand (gen sg)

sections.heading: Note
items: Russian stress sometimes behaves like it lost a bet. Most learners just absorb stress through extensive listening rather than memorizing rules.
